paragraphs: Kohl's Corporation (the "Company," "Kohl's," "we," "our," or "us") was organized in 1988 and is a Wisconsin corporation. As of January 31, 2026, we operated 1,153 Kohl's stores and a website (www.Kohls.com). Our Kohl's stores and website sell moderately-priced proprietary and national brand apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty, and home products. Our Kohl's stores generally carry a consistent merchandise assortment with some differences attributable to local preferences and store size. Our website includes merchandise which is available in our stores, as well as merchandise that is available only online.

Our merchandise mix includes both national brands and proprietary brands that are available only at Kohl's. Our proprietary portfolio includes well-known established brands such as Apt. 9, Croft & Barrow, FLX, Jumping Beans, SO, Sonoma Goods for Life, and Tek Gear, and exclusive brands that are developed and marketed through agreements with nationally-recognized brands such as LC Lauren Conrad, Nine West, and Simply Vera Vera Wang. Compared to national brands, proprietary brands generally have lower selling prices, but higher gross margins.

For discussion of our financial results, see Item 7, "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

We receive substantially all of our merchandise at our nine retail distribution centers and four e-commerce fulfillment centers. A small amount of our merchandise is delivered directly to the stores by vendors or their distributors. The retail distribution centers, which are strategically located throughout the United States, ship merchandise to each store by contract carrier. Digital sales may be picked up in our stores or are shipped to the customer from a Kohl's e-commerce fulfillment center, store, or directly by a third-party vendor.
See Item 2, "Properties," for additional information about our distribution and e-commerce fulfillment centers.

At Kohl's, we strive to foster a workplace where respect, empathy, and inclusion thrive. We believe our associates are our most valuable asset and a differentiator for our business. Our teams of associates take care of each other, our customers, and the communities we serve. We support our associates by fostering a safe and healthy work environment, offering competitive total compensation and benefits, including many health and wellness offerings, providing ongoing training and development opportunities, and cultivating a culture where all associates feel a sense of belonging and appreciation.

During 2025, we employed an average of approximately 84,000 associates, which included approximately 29,000 full-time and 55,000 part-time associates. The number of associates varies during the year, peaking during the back-to-school and holiday seasons. None of our associates are represented by a collective bargaining unit. We believe we maintain positive relationships with our associates.

We lead initiatives that ensure the way we communicate, work, and develop our product enables our customers and associates to shop, work, and engage in a safe environment. We have a team dedicated to defining plans and preparing for business crisis events, including natural disasters and other unplanned disruptions. To keep a healthy workforce, we maintain an advocacy program that provides associates with 24/7 access to medical professionals following a work accident. We continue to pursue innovative ways to educate our teams on safety. Associates at our stores, distribution, and e-commerce fulfillment centers receive specialized training to enhance our safety culture and reduce associate accidents.

At Kohl's, one of our priorities as a company is to reflect our values of being a welcoming, respectful, and inclusive company for all of our associates and all of the customers we serve. We believe that an inclusive and productive workforce that serves a broad base of customers will help drive our business forward. We are committed to our inclusion and belonging strategy, which focuses on Our People, Our Customers, and Our Community.

We strive to be purposeful in attracting, growing, and engaging a workforce comprised of different backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences, which helps us serve a broad base of customers. We are committed to cultivating a strong sense of connection and engagement within our eight Business Resource Groups (BRGs), which encompass more than 8,500 unique members and are a key component in recognizing and fostering our culture of inclusion and belonging. Our BRGs are inherently inclusive because they are open to all associates by welcoming all allies, not just the community they represent. They were created based on employee feedback and help drive business insights.

We believe our leaders are responsible for strengthening, modeling, and supporting our company Values and Behaviors by promoting a culture where all associates feel seen, heard, and valued. We provide tools and resources for our leaders to help drive a welcoming, respectful and inclusive culture while also engaging associates on how this creates a competitive advantage for Kohl's.

headings: Macroeconomic, Regulatory, Legal, and External Risks
Our business is highly sensitive to general economic conditions, consumer spending levels, and/or other external conditions, which could decline.
Geopolitical instability, hostilities, and public health events could adversely affect consumer behavior and our operations.
Changes in global trade policies and the imposition of tariffs could increase our costs and disrupt our supply chain.
Evolving regulations related to ESG, climate change, and sustainability could increase our costs and impose operational restrictions.
Regulatory and legal matters could adversely affect our business operations and change financial performance.
Weather conditions, natural disasters, and the potential impacts of climate change could adversely affect consumer shopping patterns and disrupt our operations.
We may be unable to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy.
We may be unable to offer merchandise that resonates with existing customers and attracts new customers while successfully managing our inventory levels.
Our competitors could make changes to their pricing and other practices.
Our marketing and loyalty programs may be ineffective at building personalized connections with customers.
Our business is seasonal in nature, which could negatively affect our sales, revenues, operating results, and cash requirements.
The reputation and brand image of Kohl's and the brands and products we sell could be damaged.
We may be unable to attract, develop, and retain quality associates while controlling costs, which could adversely affect our operating results.
Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Data Management, and Privacy Risks
We may be unable to adequately maintain and/or update our information systems.
Our information technology projects may not yield their intended results, and our use of artificial intelligence and machine learning technology presents evolving operational and legal risks.
Supply Chain, Third Party, and Product-Related Risks
We may be unable to source merchandise in a timely and cost-effective manner.
Our vendors may not adhere to our Terms of Engagement or to applicable laws.
There may be concerns about the safety of products that we sell.
We may be unable to raise additional capital or maintain credit on favorable terms, which could constrain our operational flexibility and increase our cost of doing business.
Our capital allocation strategy may be inefficient, may not yield the anticipated returns, or may not effectively support our long-term growth.
paragraphs: This Form 10-K contains "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Words such as "believes," "anticipates," "plans," "may," "intends," "will," "should," "expects," and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements include certain statements under Management's Discussion and Analysis and Financial and Capital Allocation Outlook and may include comments about our future sales or financial performance and our plans, performance and other objectives, expectations or intentions, such as statements regarding our liquidity, debt service requirements, planned capital expenditures, future store initiatives, adequacy of capital resources and reserves, and the impact of macroeconomic events, including inflation, consumer behavior, and changes in global trade policies, such as tariffs, and our response to such events. Forward-looking statements are based on management's then current views and assumptions and, as a result, are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those projected. As such, forward-looking statements are qualified by those risk factors described below. Forward-looking statements relate to the date made, and we undertake no obligation to update them. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future.

Our sales, revenues, gross margin, expenses, and operating results could be negatively impacted by a number of factors including, but not limited to, those described below. Many of these risk factors are outside of our control. If we are not successful in managing these risks, they could have a negative impact on our sales, revenues, gross margin, expenses, and/or operating results.

Our business is sensitive to the growth of the U.S. economy and the strength of the U.S. consumer. Consumer spending habits, including demand for the merchandise we sell, are affected by various factors beyond our control, including prevailing economic conditions, inflation and measures taken to control it, consumer responses to recessionary concerns, levels of employment, salaries and wage rates, prevailing interest rates, housing costs, energy and fuel costs, income tax rates and policies, consumer perception of economic conditions, and the consumer's disposable income, credit availability, and debt levels. Our core moderate-income customer is especially sensitive to these factors. When the cost of basic necessities, such as food, fuel, and healthcare, increases, these customers often reduce their discretionary spending, which may negatively impact our results of operations. A slowdown in the U.S. economy, an uncertain economic outlook, or a decline in consumer confidence could adversely affect consumer spending habits and result in lower traffic to our physical stores and digital platforms, increased markdowns, reduced sale conversion rates, and an adverse effect on our results of operations. Because all of our physical stores are located in the United States, we are especially susceptible to deteriorations in the U.S. economy compared to more geographically diversified competitors.

Consumer confidence and purchasing power are influenced by the domestic and international political environment. The outbreak or escalation of war, or the occurrence of terrorist acts or other hostilities in or affecting the United States or our global supply chain partners, could lead to decreased consumer spending or widespread operational disruptions. Future pandemics or other public health crises could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Such events can result in government-mandated closures, limited operating hours, labor shortages, and severe disruptions to the retail industry and global logistics network. We cannot predict the occurrence, duration, or severity of any future public health events or the effectiveness of our mitigation strategies in response to such major disruptions.

The majority of goods we source are manufactured outside of the United States, primarily in Asia. Consequently, our business is subject to risks associated with foreign trade, including changes in trade policy. Recent or potential impositions of new or increased tariffs on imported products, or the removal of de minimis thresholds for direct-to-consumer imports, could increase our merchandise costs and have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, and liquidity. On February 20, 2026, the United States Supreme Court issued a ruling striking down certain tariffs previously imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). While this ruling may lead to potential refunds, the availability, timing, and amount of such refunds remain uncertain and subject to further legal and administrative developments. Following this decision, the U.S. presidential administration announced the invocation of alternative authorities to impose new tariffs on imports from various countries. If we are unable to diversify our sourcing, divert production or sourcing away from specific countries to avoid tariffs, or successfully implement pricing actions to offset these costs, our gross margins, costs of merchandise sold, results of operations, and competitive position could be adversely affected. Furthermore, retaliatory trade measures by other countries could increase the costs of our operations or limit our access to critical raw materials or merchandise.

We are subject to income and other taxes in the United States and various local jurisdictions, and changes in tax laws or the interpretation of existing laws could increase our tax liabilities and impact our financial results.

paragraphs: Kohl's is a leading omnichannel retailer operating 1,153 stores and a website (www.Kohls.com) as of January 31, 2026. Our Kohl's stores and website sell moderately-priced proprietary and national brand apparel, footwear, accessories, beauty, and home products. Our Kohl's stores generally carry a consistent merchandise assortment with some differences attributable to local preferences and store size. Our website includes merchandise which is available in our stores, as well as merchandise that is available only online.
Key financial results for 2025 as compared to 2024 include:
• Net sales decreased 4.0%, to $14.8 billion, with comparable sales down 3.1%.
• Gross margin as a percent of net sales was 37.5%, an increase of 34 basis points.

• Selling, general & administration ("SG&A") expenses decreased 4.1% year-over-year, to $5.1 billion. As a percentage of total revenue, SG&A expenses were 32.8%, an increase of 5 basis points year-over-year.
• Gain on legal settlement was $129 million from a credit card interchange fee lawsuit settlement.
• Operating income was $624 million compared to $433 million in the prior year. As a percentage of total revenue, operating income was 4.0%, an increase of 135 basis points year-over-year.

• On an adjusted non-GAAP basis, our adjusted operating income was $510 million compared to $509 million in the prior year.(a) As a percentage of total revenue, adjusted operating income was 3.3% compared to 3.1% in the prior year.(a)
• Net income was $272 million, or $2.38 per diluted share. This compares to net income of $109 million, or $0.98 per diluted share in the prior year.

• On an adjusted non-GAAP basis, our adjusted net income was $186 million, or $1.62 per adjusted diluted share.(a) This compares to adjusted non-GAAP net income of $167 million, or $1.50 per adjusted diluted share in the prior year.(a)
• Cash flow provided by operating activities was $1.4 billion compared to $648 million in the prior year.
• Current portion of long-term debt was reduced by $353 million through repayment of the 4.25% notes due July 2025 at maturity.
• There were no outstanding borrowings under the revolving credit facility compared to $290 million in the prior year.

• Long term debt increased $262 million through issuance of $360 million of 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030, partially offset by open market repurchases of $87 million of our outstanding long term debt.

paragraphs: Kohl's Corporation (the "Company," "Kohl's," "we," "our," or "us") 於 1988 年成立，為威斯康辛州公司。截至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，本公司經營 1,153 家 Kohl's 經銷店與網站 (www.Kohls.com)。本公司 Kohl's 經銷店與網站銷售價格適中之自有品牌與國際建品牌服飾、鞋類、配件、美容與家用品。本公司 Kohl's 經銷店通常提供一致的商品種類，部分差異係因當地偏好與經銷店規模所致。本公司網站包含可供經銷店銷售之商品，以及僅於線上銷售之商品。

本公司商品組合包含國際建品牌與僅於 Kohl's 可見之自有品牌。本公司自有品牌組合包含知名已建立品牌，如 Apt. 9、Croft & Barrow、FLX、Jumping Beans、SO、Sonoma Goods for Life 與 Tek Gear，以及透過與 nationally-recognized 品牌簽約開發與行銷之獨家品牌，如 LC Lauren Conrad、Nine West 與 Simply Vera Vera Wang。相較於國際建品牌，自有品牌通常具有較低之銷售價格，但較高之毛利率。

本公司 substantially all 之商品係透過九個零售物流中心與四個電商履行中心取得。本公司少數商品係由供應商或其經銷商直接送達經銷店。零售物流中心位於美國各戰略位置，透過 contract carrier 將商品送達各經銷店。數位銷售商品可於本公司經銷店提領，或由 Kohl's 電商履行中心、經銷店或第三方供應商直接送達客戶。
有關本公司物流與電商履行中心之更多資訊，請參閱第 2 項 "財產。"
在 Kohl's，我們致力於營造一個尊重、同理心與包容並存的工作環境。我們相信我們的同仁是我們最寶貴的資產，也是我們業務的差異化因素。我們的同仁團隊會照顧彼此、顧客以及我們所服務的社區。我們透過營造安全健康的作業環境、提供具有競爭力的總報酬與福利，包括許多健康與 wellness 項目、提供持續的培訓與發展機會，以及培養一種讓所有同仁感到歸屬與被重視的文化，來支持我們的同仁。
在 2025 年，我們平均僱用了約 84,000 名同仁，其中包括約 29,000 名全職與 55,000 名兼職同仁。同仁人數會隨著年度而有所變動，尤其在回校季與節日季節達到高峯。我們的同仁並未加入任何集體談判單位。我們相信我們與同仁之間維持著正面的關係。

我們推動各種倡議，確保我們的溝通方式、作業方式與產品開發方式，能讓顧客與同仁在安全的環境中購物、工作與參與。我們有一支專門團隊負責制定計畫並準備應對業務危機事件，包括自然災害及其他未預期的中斷。為維持健康的 workforce，我們維持一個倡議計畫，讓同仁在工作事故後可 24/7 聯繫醫療專業人員。我們持續尋求創新方式來教育我們的團隊關於安全。我們的商店、物流與電商履行中心的同仁會接受專門的培訓，以強化我們的安全文化並減少同仁事故。
在 Kohl's，我們作為一家公司的一項優先事項是反映我們的價值觀，讓所有同仁與我們服務的所有顧客都能感受到我們是一個歡迎、尊重與包容的公司。我們相信，一個包容且具生產力的 workforce，能服務廣泛的顧客羣，將有助於推動我們的業務。我們致力於我們的包容與歸屬感策略，該策略聚焦於 Our People、Our Customers 與 Our Community。

我們努力在吸引、成長與激勵一個由不同背景、觀點與生活經驗組成的 workforce 上，這有助於我們服務廣泛的顧客羣。我們致力於培養我們八個業務資源羣組（BRGs）內強烈的連結與參與感，這些羣組涵蓋超過 8,500 名獨特成員，並是我們認知與培育包容與歸屬感文化的重要組成部分。我們的 BRGs 內在上是包容的，因為它們對所有同仁開放，歡迎所有盟友，而不僅僅是他們所代表的社區。這些羣組是根據員工反饋所建立，並協助推動業務洞察。
我們相信我們的領導者有責任強化、 modelling 與支持我們公司的價值觀與行為，透過促進一種讓所有同仁感到被看見、被聽見與被重視的文化。我們為領導者提供工具與資源，協助他們驅動一個歡迎、尊重與包容的文化，同時也讓同仁瞭解這如何為 Kohl's 帶來競爭優勢。

paragraphs: Kohl's 為一家領導的全通路零售商，截至2026年1月31日，經營1,153間門市與網站（www.Kohls.com）。我們的Kohl's 門市與網站銷售價格適中之自有品牌與國際建品牌服飾、鞋類、配件、美容與家用品。我們的Kohl's 門市通常提供一致的商品種類，部分差異係因應當地偏好與門市規模而有所不同。我們的網站包含門市內可購買的商品，以及僅能在網路上購買的商品。
2025年關鍵財務結果與2024年比較如下：
• 淨銷售額減少4.0%，至14.8 十億美元，其中可比銷售額減少3.1%。
• 毛利率佔淨銷售額百分比為37.5%，較前一年增加34 基點。
• 銷售、一般及行政費用（"SG&A"）減少4.1% 年增年減，至5.1 十億美元。費用佔總營業收入百分比為32.8%，較前一年增加5 基點。
• 法律和解獲利為129 百萬美元，來自信用卡交換費用訴訟和解。
• 營運收入為624 百萬美元，較前一年的433 百萬美元增加。營運收入佔總營業收入百分比為4.0%，較前一年增加135 基點。
• 依調整後非GAAP 標準，我們的調整後營運收入為510 百萬美元，較前一年的509 百萬美元略增。(a) 調整後營運收入佔總營業收入百分比為3.3%，較前一年的3.1% 略增。(a)
• 營業收入為 272 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 2.38 美元。與前一年度的營業收入 109 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後普通股 0.98 美元相比。
• 以調整後非GAAP為基準，我們的調整後營業收入為 186 百萬美元，或每股調整後稀釋普通股 1.62 美元。(a) 與前一年度的調整後非GAAP營業收入 167 百萬美元，或每股調整後稀釋普通股 1.50 美元相比。(a)
• 來自營運活動的現金流為 1.4 十億美元，與前一年度的 648 百萬美元相比。
• 長期負債的現有部分透過償還 4.25% 的票面利率到期日為 2025 年 7 月的票據，減少 353 百萬美元。
• 與前一年度的 290 百萬美元相比，本年度未有未償還的循環信貸設施貸款。
• 長期負債增加 262 百萬美元，透過發行 360 百萬美元的 10.000% 高級 secured 票據，到期日為 2030 年，部分抵銷了公開市場上 87 百萬美元的長期負債買回。

headings: 總體經濟、法規、法律及外部風險
本公司業務對總體經濟狀況、消費者支出水平及/或其他外部條件高度敏感，這些條件可能下降。
地緣政治不穩定、敵對行動及公共衛生事件可能不利於消費者行為及本公司營運。
全球貿易政策的變化及關稅的實施可能增加本公司成本並幹擾本公司供應鏈。
與環境、社會及治理（ESG）、氣候變遷及永續性相關的法規變化可能增加本公司成本並施加營運限制。
法規及法律事項可能不利於本公司業務營運並影響財務表現。
天氣條件、自然災害及氣候變遷的潛在影響可能不利於消費者購物模式並幹擾本公司營運。
本公司可能無法成功執行多渠道策略。
本公司可能無法提供能引起現有客戶共鳴並吸引新客戶的商品，同時成功管理存貨水準。
競爭對手可能對其價格及其他作法進行變更。
本公司行銷及忠誠度方案可能無法有效建立與客戶的個人化連結。
本公司業務具有季節性，這可能會對銷售額、營業收入、營運結果及現金需求產生負面影響。
Kohl's 以及本公司所銷售的品牌與產品的聲譽與品牌形象可能受到損害。
本公司可能無法在控制成本的同時吸引、培養及留住優質員工，這可能會對營運結果產生不利影響。

paragraphs: 本表單 10-K 含有根據 1995 年私人訴訟改革法案所定義之「向前看」陳述。用語如「相信」、「預期」、「計畫」、「可能」、「意圖」、「將」、「應該」、「預期」等，係用以識別向前看陳述。向前看陳述包含管理層討論與分析及財務與資本配置展望部分之某些陳述，並可能包含有關我們未來銷售或財務表現，以及我們計畫、表現及其他目標、預期或意圖之評論，例如有關我們流動性、債務償還需求、計畫資本支出、未來商店計畫、資本資源與準備金是否充足，以及總體經濟事件之影響，包括通貨膨脹、消費者行為及全球貿易政策之變動，例如關稅，以及我們對這些事件之回應。向前看陳述係根據管理層當時之觀點與假設，因此可能受到某些風險與不確定性之影響，導致實際結果與預期結果有重大差異。因此，向前看陳述已考量下列風險因素。向前看陳述係根據其發佈日期，本公司不負有更新之義務。對過往事件之參考僅為範例，並非完整清單或表示這些因素是否已過往或其未來發生之可能性。
我們之銷售、營業收入、毛利率、費用及營運結果可能受多種因素影響，包括但不限於下列所描述之因素。許多這些風險因素為我們所無法控制。若我們未能成功管理這些風險，可能對我們之銷售、營業收入、毛利率、費用及/或營運結果產生負面影響。

我們之業務對美國經濟成長與美國消費者之強度相當敏感。消費者支出習慣，包括對我們所銷售商品之需求，受多種我們無法控制之因素影響，包括當前經濟條件、通貨膨脹及控制通貨膨脹之措施、消費者對經濟衰退之擔憂反應、就業水平、薪資與工資率、當前利率、住宅成本、能源與燃料成本、所得稅率與政策、消費者對經濟條件之看法，以及消費者之可支配所得、信貸可得性與負債水平。我們之核心中等收入消費者尤其對這些因素敏感。當基本必需品，如食物、燃料與醫療保健之成本增加時，這些消費者往往會減少其自由支配支出，這可能對我們之營運結果產生負面影響。美國經濟減速、經濟展望不確定或消費者信心下降，可能對消費者支出習慣產生不利影響，導致我們實體商店與數位平台之客流量減少、折扣增加、銷售轉化率降低，並對我們之營運結果產生不利影響。因為我們所有實體商店均位於美國，我們對美國經濟衰退比地理上較分散之競爭對手更為敏感。

消費者信心與購買力受國內與國際政治環境之影響。戰爭爆發或升級、或美國或我們全球供應鏈夥伴地區發生恐怖攻擊或其他敵對行動，可能導致消費者支出減少或造成廣泛之營運中斷。未來疫情或其他公共衛生危機可能對我們之業務、財務狀況與營運結果產生重大不利影響。這些事件可能導致政府下令關閉、營運時間縮短、人力短缺，以及零售業與全球物流網路嚴重中斷。我們無法預測未來公共衛生事件之發生、持續時間或嚴重程度，亦無法預測我們對這些重大中斷之緩衝策略之有效性。

我們所採購之大多數商品係於美國境外製造，主要在亞洲。因此，我們之業務受外國貿易相關風險影響，包括貿易政策之變動。近期或潛在對進口商品課徵新或增加關稅，或取消直接對消費者進口之低價值門檻，可能提高我們之商品成本，並對我們之業務、營運結果與流動性產生重大不利影響。2026 年 2 月 20 日，美國最高法院作出裁決，廢除根據國際緊急經濟權力法案（"IEEPA"）所課徵之部分關稅。雖然此裁決可能導致潛在退款，但退款之可得性、時間與金額仍不確定，並受進一步法律與行政程序之影響。此裁決後，美國總統行政部門宣佈啟動替代權力，對來自多個國家之進口課徵新關稅。若我們無法分散採購、將生產或採購轉移至特定國家以外以避免關稅，或成功實施價格措施以抵銷這些成本，我們之毛利率、商品銷售成本、營運結果與競爭地位可能受到不利影響。此外，其他國家之報復性貿易措施可能提高我們之營運成本或限制我們對關鍵原材料或商品之取得。
我們需繳納美國及各地方司法管轄區之所得及其他稅款，稅法之變更或現有法律之解釋方式改變，可能增加我們之稅務負擔，並影響我們之財務結果。
